questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moving with uniform acceleration along a straight line covers 6 m, 10 m and 14 m in successive seconds of its motion. Its initial velocity and acceleration are respectively:
questions.explanation: For uniform acceleration, displacement in nth second is sₙ = u + a(2n−1)/2. Given s₁=6, s₂=10: subtracting yields a = 4 m/s². Substituting back: u + 2 = 6 → u = 2 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The dimensional formula [ML²T⁻²A⁻²] corresponds to which physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Energy stored in an inductor is U = ½LI². Hence L = U/I², giving dimensions [ML²T⁻²]/[A²] = [ML²T⁻²A⁻²].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform disc of mass M and radius R is rotating with angular velocity ω about its axis. Another disc of mass M and radius R/2, initially at rest, is dropped coaxially onto it. The final angular velocity of the combined system is:
questions.explanation: I₁ = ½MR². I₂ = ½M(R/2)² = MR²/8. By conservation of angular momentum: I₁ω = (I₁+I₂)ω_f → ω_f = (½)/(½+⅛)ω = (4/5)ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A satellite orbits Earth in a circular orbit with speed v. The escape velocity from this orbit is:
questions.explanation: Orbital speed v = √(GM/r). Escape velocity from that radius is v_esc = √(2GM/r) = √2 × √(GM/r) = √2 v.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One mole of a monoatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) initially at pressure P and volume V is compressed adiabatically to a volume V/8. The final pressure is:
questions.explanation: For an adiabatic process PV^γ = constant. P₂ = P₁(V₁/V₂)^γ = P(8)^(5/3) = P × (2³)^(5/3) = P × 2⁵ = 32P.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A thin ring of radius R carries a uniform charge Q. The distance from the center along the axis where the electric field magnitude is maximum is:
questions.explanation: On the axis of a charged ring, E = kQx/(x²+R²)^(3/2). Maximizing with respect to x gives x = R/√2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a metre bridge experiment, resistances of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are placed in the two gaps. The balancing length from the left end is 40 cm. If the 4 Ω resistor is shunted with another 4 Ω resistor, the shift in the balance point is:
questions.explanation: Originally: 4/6 = l/(100−l) → l = 40 cm. After shunting, 4∥4 = 2 Ω. New balance: 2/6 = l′/(100−l′) → l′ = 25 cm. Shift = 40 − 25 = 15 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A proton and a deuteron, each having the same kinetic energy, enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to their velocities. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths (r_proton : r_deuteron) is:
questions.explanation: Radius r = √(2mK)/qB. For same K and q: r ∝ √m. Since m_deuteron = 2m_proton, the ratio is 1 : √2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two long coaxial solenoids of length l, with N₁ and N₂ turns and cross-sectional area A, carry currents I₁ and I₂. Their mutual inductance is:
questions.explanation: Flux linkage in solenoid 2 due to current in 1 is N₂(μ₀N₁I₁/l)A. Hence M = N₂Φ₂/I₁ = μ₀N₁N₂A/l.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm and a concave lens of focal length 10 cm are placed coaxially 15 cm apart. An object is placed 30 cm from the convex lens. The final image is formed:
options: 15/7 cm to the right of the convex lens
30 cm to the right of the convex lens
15 cm to the left of the convex lens
questions.explanation: For convex: 1/v₁ = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60 → v₁ = 60 cm. For concave, the image acts as a virtual object at 45 cm to its right. Using 1/s + 1/s′ = 1/f with f = −10 cm and s = −45 cm gives s′ = −90/7 cm. Thus the image lies 15 − 90/7 = 15/7 cm to the right of the convex lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a photoelectric experiment, light of wavelength 200 nm ejects photoelectrons that are stopped by a retarding potential of 2 V. The threshold wavelength of the metal is approximately: (hc ≈ 1240 eV·nm)
questions.explanation: Photon energy E = 1240/200 = 6.2 eV. Work function φ = E − eV_s = 6.2 − 2 = 4.2 eV. Threshold λ₀ = 1240/4.2 ≈ 295 nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An open organ pipe of length 1.0 m resonates with fundamental frequency 340 Hz. The speed of sound in air is:
questions.explanation: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f = v/2L. Hence v = 2Lf = 2 × 1.0 × 340 = 680 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Passage: A body of mass m falls from rest under gravity in a medium exerting a resistive force kv proportional to its velocity. Q13: The terminal velocity of the body is:
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, resistive force balances weight: kv_t = mg → v_t = mg/k.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Passage (cont.): The velocity of the body as a function of time t is:
questions.explanation: From m(dv/dt) = mg − kv, separation of variables and integration with v(0)=0 yields v(t) = (mg/k)(1 − e^(−kt/m)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Passage (cont.): The distance fallen by the body when its speed reaches one-half of the terminal speed is:
questions.explanation: Setting v = v_t/2 gives t = (m/k)ln2. Integrating v(t) from 0 to this time yields x = (m²g/k²)(ln2 − 1/2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of radial nodes in a 3p orbital is:
questions.explanation: Radial nodes = n − l − 1 = 3 − 1 − 1 = 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of HO−CH₂−CH₂−COOH is:
questions.explanation: The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid (−COOH), which gets C-1. The hydroxyl group is on C-3. Hence the name is 3-hydroxypropanoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A buffer solution contains 0.1 M CH₃COOH and 0.2 M CH₃COONa. If pKₐ of acetic acid is 4.74, the pH of the buffer is:
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKₐ + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.74 + log(0.2/0.1) = 4.74 + 0.30 = 5.04.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The molar conductivity of a 0.1 M weak acid solution is 10 S cm² mol⁻¹. If its limiting molar conductivity is 400 S cm² mol⁻¹, the degree of dissociation is:
questions.explanation: Degree of dissociation α = Λ_m/Λ° = 10/400 = 0.025.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following alcohols reacts fastest with Lucas reagent at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Lucas test distinguishes alcohols based on carbocation stability. tert-Butanol forms a 3° carbocation most readily and reacts fastest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Among the following ions, which has the maximum number of unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: Electronic configurations: Cr³⁺ (3d³) → 3 unpaired, Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) → 5 unpaired, Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) → 4 unpaired, Co²⁺ (3d⁷) → 3 unpaired. Hence Mn²⁺ has the maximum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2-bromo-2-methylbutane on treatment with alcoholic KOH at 80 °C mainly gives:
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH promotes E2 elimination. The substrate is a tertiary bromide; elimination follows Saytzeff’s rule to give the more substituted alkene, 2-methyl-2-butene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a reaction at 300 K, ΔH° = −40 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS° = −100 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. The equilibrium constant K is approximately:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is commonly used as an antacid?
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a basic salt that neutralizes excess stomach acid and is a common antacid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The complex [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic. The hybridization of Co in this complex is:
questions.explanation: Co³⁺ is d⁶. NH₃ is a strong field ligand causing low-spin t₂g⁶eg⁰ configuration. The complex is diamagnetic and inner orbital, so hybridization is d²sp³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a measure of:
questions.explanation: BOD quantifies the amount of oxygen required by aerobic microorganisms to decompose biodegradable organic material in a water sample.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Passage: An aqueous solution of CuSO₄ is electrolyzed for 9650 s using a current of 2 A with platinum electrodes. Q27: The mass of copper deposited at the cathode is: (F ≈ 96500 C mol⁻¹, Cu = 63.5 g mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Q = It = 2 × 9650 = 19300 C. Moles of electrons = 19300/96500 = 0.2 mol. Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, so moles of Cu = 0.1. Mass = 0.1 × 63.5 = 6.35 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Passage (cont.): If copper electrodes are used instead of platinum, the mass of the anode:
questions.explanation: With a copper anode, Cu dissolves as Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻. For every mole of Cu deposited at the cathode, one mole dissolves from the anode. Hence the anode mass decreases by 6.35 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Passage (cont.): The volume of O₂ gas liberated at STP at the platinum anode during the same electrolysis is:
questions.explanation: At the Pt anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. Moles of O₂ = (moles e⁻)/4 = 0.2/4 = 0.05 mol. Volume at STP = 0.05 × 22.4 = 1.12 L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Passage (cont.): If the initial solution contained 0.5 mol of CuSO₄ in 500 mL, the concentration of Cu²⁺ remaining after electrolysis is:
questions.explanation: Initial moles of Cu²⁺ = 0.5 mol. Moles deposited = 0.1 mol. Remaining Cu²⁺ = 0.4 mol in 0.5 L, giving concentration = 0.4/0.5 = 0.8 M.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The number of relations that can be defined on a set containing 3 elements is:
questions.explanation: A relation is a subset of A × A. If |A| = 3, then |A × A| = 9. Number of subsets = 2⁹ = 512.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If sinθ + cosθ = 1/2, then the value of sin2θ is:
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides: sin²θ + cos²θ + 2sinθcosθ = 1/4 → 1 + sin2θ = 1/4 → sin2θ = −3/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The function f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 1 is decreasing in the interval:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The middle term in the expansion of (x + 1/x)^10 is:
questions.explanation: There are 11 terms; the middle term is T₆ = ¹⁰C₅ x⁵ (1/x)⁵ = ¹⁰C₅ = 252.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The equation of a circle that touches both coordinate axes in the first quadrant and has radius 5 is:
questions.explanation: A circle touching both axes in the first quadrant with radius 5 has center at (5, 5). Its equation is (x−5)² + (y−5)² = 25.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The value of ∫₀^π (x sinx)/(1 + cos²x) dx is:
questions.explanation: Using ∫₀^a f(x)dx = ∫₀^a f(a−x)dx and adding, 2I = π∫₀^π sinx/(1+cos²x)dx. Substituting u = cosx gives 2I = π²/2, so I = π²/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If |a + b| = |a − b|, then the angle between vectors a and b is:
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides: |a|² + |b|² + 2a·b = |a|² + |b|² − 2a·b → 4a·b = 0 → a·b = 0. Hence the angle is π/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers on the upper faces is divisible by 4 is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²) = [1 + (dy/dx)²]^(3/2) is:
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides to eliminate the radical gives (d²y/dx²)² = [1 + (dy/dx)²]³. The highest derivative is d²y/dx² and its highest power is 2. Hence degree = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If a line makes equal angles with the coordinate axes, its direction cosines are:
questions.explanation: If α = β = γ, then cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1 → 3cos²α = 1 → cosα = ±1/√3. In the first octant, direction cosines are 1/√3, 1/√3, 1/√3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If A is a 3×3 matrix with |A| = 5, then |2A| equals:
questions.explanation: For an n×n matrix, |kA| = kⁿ|A|. Here |2A| = 2³ × 5 = 8 × 5 = 40.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If ω is a complex cube root of unity, then (1+ω)(1+ω²)(1+ω⁴)(1+ω⁸) equals:
questions.explanation: Since ω³ = 1, we have ω⁴ = ω and ω⁸ = ω². The product becomes [(1+ω)(1+ω²)]² = [1+ω+ω²+ω³]² = [0+1]² = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The sum to infinity of the series 1 + 2/3 + 4/9 + 8/27 + ... is:
questions.explanation: This is a geometric series with first term a = 1 and common ratio r = 2/3. Sum = a/(1−r) = 1/(1/3) = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Passage (cont.): The probability P(X > 1) is:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Detoxification of drugs and alcohol in liver cells is primarily carried out by the:
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) contains enzymes that detoxify drugs, alcohol, and other metabolic poisons.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. The possible blood groups of their children are:
questions.explanation: The man is IᴬIᴮ and the woman is ii. The children can inherit either Iᴬ or Iᴮ from the father and i from the mother, giving genotypes Iᴬi (blood group A) and Iᴮi (blood group B).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which ecological pyramid is always upright, regardless of the ecosystem?
questions.explanation: The pyramid of energy is always upright because energy decreases at successive trophic levels due to metabolic losses. Pyramids of numbers and biomass can sometimes be inverted.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gibberellins are plant hormones that primarily promote:
questions.explanation: Gibberellins stimulate stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering. Fruit ripening is promoted by ethylene, and leaf abscission by abscisic acid/ethylene.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In human blood, bicarbonate ions (HCO₃⁻) primarily function as:
options: A buffer system and transport form of CO₂
questions.explanation: Bicarbonate serves as the principal blood buffer (resisting pH changes) and transports about 70% of CO₂ from tissues to lungs as dissolved bicarbonate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a PCR reaction, two primers have melting temperatures (Tₘ) of 62 °C and 68 °C. The optimal annealing temperature is closest to:
questions.explanation: The annealing temperature is typically set 3–5 °C below the lower Tₘ to ensure both primers bind specifically without mismatches. Here, 62 − 4 = 58 °C.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Industrial melanism observed in the peppered moth (Biston betularia) is a classic example of:
questions.explanation: Industrial melanism represents directional selection, where pollution darkens tree trunks and selects for the dark (carbonaria) morph over the light morph.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In human females, meiosis II is completed:
options: After entry of the sperm into the ovum
questions.explanation: Meiosis I completes before ovulation, but meiosis II arrests at metaphase until fertilization. It is only completed after a sperm enters the secondary oocyte.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: Maltose has a free anomeric carbon and can reduce Tollens'/Fehling's reagents. Sucrose (glucose α-1,2-fructose) lacks a free hemiacetal and is non-reducing.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A dihybrid cross yields a modified phenotypic ratio of 9 : 3 : 4. This indicates:
questions.explanation: The 9:3:4 ratio arises when a homozygous recessive genotype at one locus masks the expression of another locus (recessive epistasis), as seen in coat color in mice or flower color in sweet peas.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Biological nitrogen fixation in root nodules of legumes is performed by:
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live symbiotically in legume root nodules, where they differentiate into bacteroids that fix atmospheric N₂ into ammonia using the nitrogenase enzyme.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passage: In a population of 10,000 individuals, the frequency of the recessive phenotype (aa) is 16%. Q57: The frequency of the recessive allele (a) is:
questions.explanation: Recessive phenotype frequency = q² = 0.16. Therefore q = √0.16 = 0.40.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passage (cont.): The number of heterozygous individuals (Aa) in the population is approximately:
questions.explanation: p = 1 − q = 0.60. Heterozygote frequency = 2pq = 2 × 0.60 × 0.40 = 0.48. Number of Aa individuals = 0.48 × 10,000 = 4800.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passage (cont.): If heterozygotes have 20% higher fitness than either homozygote, the frequency of allele a after many generations will:
questions.explanation: With symmetric heterozygote advantage, balancing selection maintains both alleles in the population. The stable equilibrium frequency for each allele is 0.5, so q will rise from 0.4 toward 0.5.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Passage (cont.): This type of natural selection, which maintains multiple alleles in a population, is called:
questions.explanation: Balancing selection includes heterozygote advantage (overdominance), frequency-dependent selection, and heterogeneous environments, all of which preserve genetic variation.
